Homer Turned It Into Myth. A Deleted Scripture Filed the Report First.

Nobody watching Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey walks out confused about why the sirens scene works. Reviewers called it the hardest scene in the whole poem to put on screen, and most agree Nolan solved it by making you watch a disciplined man come apart instead of asking you to believe an actress can out-sing seduction itself.

What nobody explained is why it feels older than the direction. Why it plays like memory, not performance.

That’s strange, for a myth. Myths are supposed to feel invented. This one feels remembered.

Homer wrote it down in the eighth century BC. He gives you the meadow, the bones, the promise. He never tells you what she is, where she came from, or why the sound of her would already feel like something you’d heard before.

So what is a siren, exactly?

Ask a professor and the answers start contradicting each other before you finish the question. Half-bird in the early vase paintings. Daughters of the river god Achelous, in one tradition. Companions of Persephone, cursed with wings for failing to stop her kidnapping, in another. Three traditions. Not one of them agrees on what she actually is.

Ask a Pastor and you’ll get nothing. Sirens are Greek. They’re myth. Not his department. File it under stories people used to tell.

No source. Just the effect.

Except there is a source. The New Testament quotes it. Ethiopia still reads it as Scripture. And it isn’t in your Bible.

Three witnesses, no coordination

Here’s the problem with calling it myth. Myths are supposed to be things invented independently by different cultures, who then proceed to tell different stories about the same vague idea.

Ask then, why the Septuagint, a Jewish Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible made three centuries before Christ, and containing no interest in appealing to Greek polytheism, renders the word nephilim in Genesis 6:4 as gigantes, the exact Greek word for beings born of a god and a mortal woman, and not as something else.

Ask why one of the earliest Christian defenses of the faith, a document addressed to the Roman Senate by the man who would soon be martyred for his trouble, contains a whole chapter arguing that Zeus, Neptune, and Pluto are not gods at all, but angels and the demons those angels fathered, wrongly credited as gods, and why the author, Justin Martyr, writing around AD 160, names them specifically, and why he never uses the word nephilim, assuming his reader knows what he means without him having to say it.

Ask why a Hebrew text with no interest in Greek mythology, a Greek translation with no stake in Greek poetry at all, and a Christian text arguing that the gods of the Greeks are actually angels who sinned and fell, whose children by mortal women are the demons behind the myth, all contain the same story, without ever having to coordinate.

Coincidence has to explain that three times over.

The Sentence

1 Enoch 19:1-2, R.H. Charles translation: the angel Uriel is walking Enoch through the judgment site, showing him exactly where each group of the fallen will stand when the reckoning comes. He gets to the Watchers’ wives last:

“And the women also of the angels who went astray shall become sirens.”

Become sirens, not become like sirens.

The women who had been taken up to Mount Hermon along with their husbands the Watchers are not forgotten about when the flood comes, but get a specific punishment for their part in the events, a name for what they become.

The children of that same union get their own name too, in the Septuagint’s rendering of Genesis 6: gigantes, the same word Homer and Hesiod already used for their own heroes and monsters. Two separate translators, working on two separate texts, reaching for the same vocabulary without ever comparing notes.

The events described in 1 Enoch do not take place at the same time as the flood. The angels fall from heaven and take up their residence in the earth long before “the deluge” comes, and long before anyone takes up a sword against Troy.

If Justin Martyr is right, then Homer is not inventing things when he talks of the monsters and gods of his poetry, but rather transcribing real events which happened long before his time, and which the Greeks had turned into myth.

If that is not the case, then neither is it a coincidence that Homer uses the same word for the giants begotten of gods and men as the Septuagint does in its rendering of Genesis 6, nor that 1 Enoch says the women who took part in this ancient sin will become sirens.

The Aeneas problem

So how does a book quoted in the New Testament vanish from the West for centuries?

The reason is simple. Rome told its founding story through Troy. Aeneas escapes the burning city, sails west, and the line he starts eventually produces Romulus, who founds Rome generations later. Troy is, as you might guess, the setting for Homer’s other great work, the Iliad, and the war there is the one Odysseus is returning from when he runs into Circe.

The city that would host the councils deciding your Bible’s contents located its own origins inside the same story Homer was telling. And Rome could not accept that the gods carved into its temples were fallen angels, or that the divine parentage running through its founding story belonged to the same category of event 1 Enoch was describing.

You cannot canonize a book which names your emperor’s ancestors as fallen angels and expect that emperor to fund your church.

There’s another reason.

Circe drugs Odysseus’s crew into animals. That’s pharmakeia, sorcery worked through substance, and it’s on the list of what the Watchers taught men in 1 Enoch’s opening chapters. Once a Roman convert sees that, the whole system of paganism stops looking like ordinary custom you can baptize and absorb. It starts looking like the same thing still running under new names.

It starts looking like the same curriculum under new management, where what Justin calls fallen angels, Rome calls gods. Once the convert can name the source, he can’t walk past a temple without reading it.

Rome needed pagan gods to be fiction, myth, a convenient delusion which could be overcome by a better one. It couldn’t afford them to be an open case with a source, with named perpetrators.

So the book which gave the source and the name had to go.

Two witnesses

Two witnesses kept the file open. Ethiopia never had a reason to close it. The canon of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church was set down long before the final decisions in the west, and it never had the same incentive to remove 1 Enoch, which it continued to read as scripture up until today. If the book was too fantastic to be included, Ethiopia had every reason to exclude it as well. It didn’t.

And before the rest of Rome closed the file, its strongest defenders were still inside it. Justin Martyr was not writing in a vacuum when he told the Roman Senate that Neptune and Pluto were angels, and the demons they fathered, mistaken for gods.

Tertullian and Athenagoras followed him, making similar arguments about demons as the source of paganism, rather than outright declaring it false.

They are not obscure theologians who later Christianity has forgotten. They are Church Fathers, whose writings are still remembered, who still have influence, who are writing in the same tradition. This is why the file was never truly closed. It was kept open by the men who needed it most, and it was closed later, when that need was gone.

Go read the Second Apology yourself, and see what Justin Martyr told the Roman Senate about the source of his gods. He assumed they knew it, and in his day, they probably did. You don’t know it, and you never learned it in Sunday school, which is why this is not an accident of transmission. It’s an edit.

Rome needed Zeus to be fiction, it needed its own bloodline, the one traced back to Aeneas, to be foundation rather than evidence. The drugs are just one part of a much longer list, and the list is still in the file. Homer gave you the sound of her. Enoch gave you her name.

That list doesn’t stop at pharmakeia. Azazel brought down weapons, cosmetics, astrology, genetic manipulation, the rest is already filed. Subscribe and keep reading the case Rome closed.
